Commentary.Commentary: Now, one thing is for sure, England will play their shots and will probably go for quick runs. Jacks did mention today morning they will be looking for a win irrespective of the situation so it will be interesting to see what will be their aim. Saying that, the style with which England plays could bring about wickets for Pakistan and that could well see them in a position from where they can think of a win. However, they will be without Rauf who won't be bowling in this game. Can the others step up? We will find out.

For the England bowlers, just like their opposition, it was a hard toil. Will Jacks was the star with the six-fer on debut and he was well-supported by Jack Leach! Ollie Robinson was also impressive as he really bowled with all his heart. James Anderson was tidy. England too will be happy with their overall effort but would have loved a bigger lead especially after the position they started off on Day 4.

Overall, Pakistan did a decent job with the bat, it was their openers who set the tone as both scored tons and added over 200. Azam continued the good work and he too scored a brilliant ton.At once, it seemed Pakistan might just take the lead but most of the batters in the middle order failed to make a significant contribution and at the end of Day 3, it seemed England would get a big lead by Agha Salman with the tail ensured that is not the case.

Pakistan will be pleased with how things went about this morning. Agha Salman played attacking cricket earlier on and got to his half ton. He along with Zahid Mahmood added fifty before Agha Salman fell. Rauf and Zahid then added a few handy runs but there was not a lot of contrubution from the last wicket stand.

England have finally managed to bundle Pakistan out! They though would have loved to have given fewer runs before getting the wickets. They have only managed to gain a lead of 78, however, the good thing is, they do have a lead. Jacks was once again the star with the ball for them this morning as he got all the three wikets to fall and in the end, ended with a six-fer.

A fine last session on Day 3 for England has really added some spark to this game. It seemed to be heading towards a dull draw but the visitors now can fancy their chances of taking a lead in this series. Pakistan still trail by over 150 and have just the three wickets left. England's first aim will be to get the remaining wickets quickly. They'll be hoping they can take a lead of over 100. Pakistan on the other hand, will be hoping the tail can wag along with Salman and get as close to England's total if not surpass it. The first session is quite an important one. Welcome to th3 coverage.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

This pitch might be flat and soft as you like but England have done really well to take 7 wickets. They took time to find the rhythm but the doors open once they got the openers. Ben Stokes was brilliant as he shuffled his pack brilliantly. The spinners, especially Will Jacks is getting some purchase. He took three wickets and also got the big wicket of Azam. Now then, two more days left. A draw is looking like the outcome result if we speak honestly but England will look to start Day 4 and look for wickets straightaway while Pakistan still trail by 158 runs and have to bet on Agha Salman to reduce it. Join us on 4th December for all the action of Day 4. The action starts at 10.15 am IST (4.45 am GMT). Till then, cheers!

So, that is the end of Day 3. We feel England will be the happier team at this stage. Still, a long way to go but this final session has just pushed England a touch on the front foot. 4 wickets fell in the final session. Pakistan started the day comfortably with both their openers out in full flow. It looked like Pakistan will give the same kind of reply but both openers fell after scoring their tons respectively. Babar Azam then played with intent and with a good rate to notch yet another ton. Pakistan were three down before the Tea break but after that lost the big names and find themselve with tail-enders to save them.

Day 2 saw Pakistan roaring back into the game! First it was their bowlers who managed to get the remaining wickets quickly and then, their openers who batted brilliantly and ensured the hosts lost no wickets. ... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The second day of the first Test match between Pakistan and England has come to an end and this has been a display of various batting styles throughout the day. There has been very little joy for the bowlers over the past two days but their time may still come. Will the hosts continue to collect runs? Or will England manage to take some early wickets and put pressure on their opponents? We shall find out when the play resumes on Saturday, 3rd of December at 10.05 am IST (4.35 am GMT). Do join us for the build-up which begins well in advance. Cheers!

Right then, Day 3 is considered the moving day of a Test match and it will be interesting to see what we have in store for us. If the pitch continues to be as flat as it has been on the first two days we do not expect there to be much moving. England will have to come out with a better strategy to break this stubborn opening partnership and they will be hoping that their fast bowlers get the old ball to reverse swing. Pakistan will be absolutely delighted as long as Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq can continue to accumulate runs and they know they have a solid middle order to add further misery to the English bowlers.

England came out all guns blazing and looked to take the attack to the Pakistani bowlers from the word go. Their approach worked initially but they lost two of their big hitters Ben Stokes and Liam Livingstone early. Harry Brook carried on to score a brisk 150 and take his team close to the 600-run mark. Ollie Robinson and Will Jacks got to their 30s but wickets fell too often which prevented them from crossing 700 which would have been their target. Naseem Shah bowled with fire and put on an inspired performance as he claimed 3 crucial wickets. Zahid Mahmood gave loads of runs away but returned with four wickets for his effort in his debut game. After that, it has been all about the Pakistan openers who batted through two sessions and are taking their team to a position of safety. Liam Livingstone suffered an injury while fielding after which he has been off for treatment. England will be hoping he can return as his bowling may come to use.

The Pakistan openers came into this session looking to bat to Stumps and build a partnership which they have managed to achieve quite comfortably. They have put on a 181-run partnership and they have not been bothered at all barring the one opportunity Abdullah Shafique offered Ollie Pope to take behind the wicket off the bowling of James Anderson. Apart from that incident, it has been plain sailing for the Pakistan batters as they looked untroubled. They are both nearing their hundreds and they will be eager to make it big on this flat pitch. England deployed the spinners for long periods in the hope to wear the ball out a bit and get it to reverse swing. None of their tactics seemed to work though and it looks like a long day in the office for the English bowlers.

SESSION SUMMARY - 18 overs, 73 runs, and 0 wickets. Another day dominated by the batters and this Test match seems to be headed in the direction of a draw unless something changes drastically. We have witnessed two contrasting styles of batting with the England players opting to go for the aggressive approach while the Pakistan batters have displayed patience and accumulated runs in a typical Test-match manner. The last two sessions have belonged to Pakistan and the fact that they claimed 6 England wickets in the first session, makes this undoubtedly a day that belongs to the hosts.

That is a close call for Abdullah Shafique! James Anderson bangs this in short and angles the ball down leg side. England will have to make some strategies for the Tea as they haven't troubled the Pakistan batters much. The wicket has nothing for the bowlers and is a graveyard for them. We shall find out. Do join us at 4.05 pm IST (10.35 am GMT) post Tea.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 91 runs, and 0 wickets. A session that finally belonged to Pakistan. Babar Azam will be extremely pleased with the performances of the two openers in this session. In 27 overs, they have gained 91 runs, but more significantly, they have not lost a wicket. The scoreboard reads 108 for no loss and Pakistan will hope to continue with the same momentum. Abdullah Shafique is on 54 whilst Imam-ul-Haq is on 52.

... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Pakistan started off slow with the bat and the openers remained unbeaten before the session break. Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq have added 17 runs and will be looking to continue the run flow after the break. England bowlers haven't troubled the Pakistan batters for the first six overs so far. Maybe Ben Stokes will try something different and get the spinners on after lunch. Can they take some early wickets in the second session? We'll find out. Do join us at 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT) post the Lunch break.

SESSION SUMMARY - 32 overs, 168 runs, and 6 wickets. With England's innings having ended on a mammoth total of 657, Pakistan have gotten off to a watchful start with their openers. Harry Brook was amazing with the bat as he scored 153 off 113 balls. England had their intent clear as they came to bat on this day and were looking to score quick runs but Pakistan's bowlers bounced back well and took 6 wickets in the first session of Day 2.
